name: functional-programming
description: Learn and apply functional programming in JavaScript and TypeScript. Refactor code into pure functions, review side effects and mutation, and understand composition and algebraic data types.

interface.longDescription:
Learn and apply functional programming in JavaScript and TypeScript. Refactor code into pure functions, work with immutable data, compose functions, and make side effects explicit while preserving existing behavior. Review code for mutation, callback arity, missing values, error handling, and asynchronous execution. Learn currying, map versus flatMap, Option/Maybe, Either/Result, functors, monads, traversal, and folds through concrete examples.

Use it to learn a concept, review a function, or refactor a codebase. It follows your project's existing libraries and conventions and does not require a new functional-programming framework. It provides instructions and examples; code execution and repository access depend on the tools available in your ChatGPT or Codex session.

Independently adapted from Professor Frisby's Mostly Adequate Guide to Functional Programming by the Mostly Adequate Core Team and contributors, with attribution and CC BY-SA 4.0 licensing. No endorsement by the original authors is implied.
defaultPrompt: Refactor this JavaScript into pure functions without changing its behavior.
Review this TypeScript for mutation, side effects, and error-handling pitfalls.
Teach me map versus flatMap with a small JavaScript example.
